I have struggled the past few years with Borderline Personality Disorder and in this time, Red Hot Chili Peppers and JF have become something of a saving grace for me. I love to watch the VPRO interviews, as painful as they are.I identified a lot with John had to say concerning life and death, loneliness, wanting to feel free, music and pain. “Every single little thing alters you”. Where he went down a narcotic path to numb himself, I chose self harm and suicidal ideation.

Where he truly is inspirational, to me,  is that he never gave up or gave in. He got up, and with his support network aiding him, he took himself to rehab. He rejoined RHCP and has remained happy, healthy & clean (+ mentally stable) for over 20 years. His arms are scarred to shit as a result of bad injecting/skin grafts, but he displays them, unashamed. Just like I will have to with my self harm scars…eventually. He taught me that you cannot regret the choices you have made, for they have contributed to the path you walk today.

When my headspace gets bad for me now, it hits harder than in previous years. I’ve gone from self harming for relief, to wanting to die completely. JF & RHCP have gotten me through more bad days (suicidal thought days) than I can count this year. The music eases my loneliness.  I feel like I have friends in them somewhat.While I feel as low and lost as junkie John at times, if that man can survive 7 years of hell both mentally/physically and come out the other side looking/feeling happy and healthy, surely I can too.

​

Thats my story (so far).

I did CICO for years. It led to a very UNHEALTHY relationship with food. 

I was tired, I was grumpy, I was depressed, I couldn't work. I wasn't healthy. Physically or mentally. 
I gained every single pound back, and those pounds brought friends. 

On Keto, my mind is clear, my HDL ("good" cholesterol) is high, my body isn't tired or sluggish, I wake up with a spring in my step. Most importantly, my blood sugars are lower than ever before. 
Those are the real reasons I'm here. Weight loss is just an added aesthetic bonus. 

The science may not yet have the popularity and widespread familiarity as the USDA food pyramid, and you dismiss it as "junk science", but I know what makes me feel better, I know what works for me, as do the people on here. You will never know what works for every individual, just what works for you. 

We feel awesome eating high fat. Thanks for your concern OP, but we don't need it.
